Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning for a Mean From the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation (AIPE) Perspective

Source: R/ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity.Rd

Evaluates a sample size plan for the confidence interval for a mean by Monte Carlo simulation. Each of G replications draws a sample of the planned (or a specified) size from the data generating population, forms the t interval, and records its width and whether it missed the true mean. The summary shows what a plan from ss_aipe_mean delivers when the planning value of the standard deviation is wrong, when the population is not normal, or both. The population is either normal, with mean true_mean and standard deviation true_sd, or the empirical distribution of a vector of observed scores, resampled with replacement, which is how a plan is checked against the skewness, tails, and discreteness of real data such as a pilot's difference scores.

Usage

ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity(
  true_sd = NULL,
  supposed_sd = NULL,
  specified_N = NULL,
  width,
  true_mean = 0,
  population = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  true_kurtosis = 0,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_sd

The data generating standard deviation of a normal population. Supply it, or population, but not both.

supposed_sd

The supposed standard deviation, the planning value passed to ss_aipe_mean to plan the sample size (not an estimate computed from data). Supply this or specified_N, but not both.

specified_N

A sample size to evaluate in place of a planned one; the planner is then bypassed. A single whole number of at least 2.

width

The desired full width of the confidence interval: the planning target, and the bound against which pct_ci_less_width counts the realized widths.

true_mean

The data generating mean of a normal population (default 0). The width does not depend on it; the misses are counted against it. Not supplied with population.

population

NULL (the default) for a normal population, or a numeric vector of scores whose empirical distribution is the population: each replication draws its sample from these scores with replacement. The true mean is then their mean and the true standard deviation their standard deviation with divisor equal to their number, the standard deviation of the distribution resampled. Missing values are refused rather than dropped.

conf_level

The confidence level of the interval (default 0.95).

assurance

NULL (the default) or the assurance passed to ss_aipe_mean when it plans the sample size; when one is supplied it is also echoed, as the value pct_ci_less_width is read against.

true_kurtosis

The planning value of the excess kurtosis passed to ss_aipe_mean (default 0), on the scale kurtosis reports. It changes the plan only together with supposed_sd and an assurance; the function warns when a nonzero value would go unused. As there, it must be greater than -2; the true_kurtosis argument of ss_aipe_mean says what to pass for a pilot whose kurtosis() is -2 or less.

G

The number of Monte Carlo replications (default 1000).

print_iter

Logical. Print the index of each replication as it runs, which is helpful in a long run; default FALSE.

filename

Optional path of a CSV file to receive the per-replication results (the sample mean and standard deviation, the interval limits and width, and the two tail misses), appended when the file already exists and created otherwise. The default NULL writes nothing; a throwaway run that wants the file should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the run reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value. The rows mean_mean, median_mean, and sd_mean summarize the G sample means; mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, and sd_ci_width summarize the interval widths; pct_ci_less_width is the proportion of intervals no wider than width, to be read against the assurance of the plan (or against a value near one half for an expected width plan); pct_ci_miss_low is the proportion of intervals lying entirely above the true mean (the true mean below the lower limit) and pct_ci_miss_high the proportion lying entirely below it, with total_type_I_error their sum. These proportions are on the 0 to 1 scale. The input echoes are total_N (the sample size evaluated), true_sd and true_mean (computed from population when one is supplied), supposed_sd (NA when specified_N was supplied instead), width, conf_level, and, when an assurance was supplied, assurance. The attribute population records whether the population was "normal" or "resampled".

Details

What each replication does. A sample of total_N scores is drawn, and the interval \(\bar{y} \pm t_{1-\alpha/2,\,N-1}\, S/\sqrt{N}\) is formed, the one t.test() reports and the one the plan was made for. Every replication returns an interval, so none is dropped. A resample whose scores are all equal, which a discrete population allows at a small N, gives an interval of zero width, and it is counted as it falls.

What to read. The width rows against width show the effect of a planning value of the standard deviation that differs from the true one: the width is proportional to \(S\), so a population standard deviation larger than the planning value widens every interval. pct_ci_less_width against the plan's assurance shows whether the plan delivered the probability it promised; with a resampled population it is the check, free of the two-moment approximation, on the planner's true_kurtosis adjustment. The two miss rows, each against \(\alpha/2\), show the coverage of the t interval in the population at hand: under normality both tails miss at the nominal rate, and a skewed population misses more often in one tail than in the other, which the plan does not address.

A pilot as the population. Passing a pilot sample's scores as population and its standard deviation as supposed_sd evaluates the plan in a population with exactly the pilot's shape, so the planning value is correct (up to the divisor) and what the simulation isolates is the effect of the shape. The pilot is itself a sample, so its shape, and above all its tails, carries sampling error of its own.

Sensitivity analysis by simulation, in which the population value that generates the data and the value the plan assumed are set separately, was introduced for the standardized mean difference by Kelley and Rausch (2006); the ss_aipe_*_sensitivity() family carries it to the other AIPE planners, with a common set of rows.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Examples

# The pilot of the ss_aipe_mean() page: the IQ gains of the 246 children
# in the control group of the pygmalion data.
gain <- pygmalion$iq_gain[pygmalion$treatment == "Control"]

# A plan for 90 percent assurance made under normal theory, evaluated by
# resampling the pilot's own gains, whose tails are heavier than the
# normal's: the share of intervals no wider than 4 points (the row
# pct_ci_less_width) falls short of .90.
ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity(supposed_sd = sd(gain), width = 4,
                         population = gain, assurance = 0.90, seed = 113)
#>  term               value 
#>  mean_mean          8.660 
#>  median_mean        8.687 
#>  sd_mean            0.928 
#>  mean_ci_width      3.736 
#>  median_ci_width    3.733 
#>  sd_ci_width        0.234 
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.870 
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.021 
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.034 
#>  total_type_I_error 0.055 
#>  total_N            195   
#>  true_sd            13.270
#>  true_mean          8.663 
#>  supposed_sd        13.297
#>  width              4     
#>  conf_level         0.950 
#>  assurance          0.900 
#> 
#> Replications: 1000
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# The plan made with the pilot's excess kurtosis is six children larger,
# and the share comes close to .90.
ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity(supposed_sd = sd(gain), width = 4,
                         population = gain, assurance = 0.90,
                         true_kurtosis = kurtosis(gain), seed = 113)
#>  term               value 
#>  mean_mean          8.657 
#>  median_mean        8.669 
#>  sd_mean            0.941 
#>  mean_ci_width      3.680 
#>  median_ci_width    3.684 
#>  sd_ci_width        0.230 
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.913 
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.025 
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.026 
#>  total_type_I_error 0.051 
#>  total_N            201   
#>  true_sd            13.270
#>  true_mean          8.663 
#>  supposed_sd        13.297
#>  width              4     
#>  conf_level         0.950 
#>  assurance          0.900 
#> 
#> Replications: 1000
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# A normal population whose standard deviation is 15 when the plan
# assumed 13.3: the realized intervals run wider than the target.
ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity(true_sd = 15, supposed_sd = 13.3, width = 4,
                         seed = 113)
#>  term               value 
#>  mean_mean          -0.003
#>  median_mean        0.023 
#>  sd_mean            1.137 
#>  mean_ci_width      4.512 
#>  median_ci_width    4.511 
#>  sd_ci_width        0.241 
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.013 
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.031 
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.021 
#>  total_type_I_error 0.052 
#>  total_N            172   
#>  true_sd            15    
#>  true_mean          0     
#>  supposed_sd        13.300
#>  width              4     
#>  conf_level         0.950 
#>
